VRT and ETN remain core direct mappings to data-center power and cooling hardware; PWR maps to grid/site delivery and construction labor; FIX maps to MEP/site execution; MOD maps to cooling/chiller capacity.

VRT, ETN, GEV, PWR, and AAON are the top five candidates for this node in the current pass because each maps directly to power/cooling/grid/site-delivery constraints and has recent evidence tied to data-center or AI infrastructure demand.

POWL should remain on the watchlist as a less obvious, more specialized medium-voltage switchgear and packaged power-systems candidate; it was not included in the top-five list only because the pass was capped at five candidates.

MOD and NVT should be tracked in the cooling/liquid-cooling sub-bucket as second-wave candidates; both appear relevant, but need deeper revenue-share and customer-concentration validation before ranking above the broader infrastructure leaders.

The node appears to split into four investable sub-buckets: critical data-center power/cooling systems, electrical gear and transformers, grid/power-generation equipment, and engineering/construction labor for interconnection and site delivery.

This pass did not fully cover data-center REITs, utilities with specific hyperscaler power contracts, private transformer suppliers, non-US-listed leaders such as Schneider Electric/ABB/Siemens Energy, or land/site developers. These require separate node-specific passes.

Add NVT as a component-level liquid-cooling, rack, power, and connection infrastructure candidate; evidence strengthened by NVIDIA/Siemens AI data-center reference architecture participation.

Add ECL as an adjacent liquid-cooling and water/fluid-management candidate contingent on CoolIT transaction close; classify as hypothesis until acquisition closes and revenue contribution is reported.

Future passes should separately screen utilities, data-center REITs, transformer manufacturers, EPC firms, copper/cable suppliers, backup power, substations, gas turbines, permitting/interconnection software, and regional land/site developers.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded universe for the AI data-center physical-infrastructure node. The highest-directness candidates are suppliers and contractors tied to power delivery, thermal management, liquid cooling, electrical/mechanical construction, and grid/data-center delivery. This is research coverage only, not a trading recommendation. Main chokepoint logic: even if AI chips are available, data-center deployment can be constrained by power equipment, cooling systems, interconnection, construction labor, and long-lead electrical infrastructure. Expanded universe for the AI data-center physical-infrastructure chokepoint. The highest-relevance US-listed candidates cluster around critical power/cooling systems, electrical gear, grid/power generation equipment, engineering/construction labor, and specialized data-center cooling. This pass prioritizes companies with observable backlog/order evidence or explicit company disclosures tying demand to data centers, AI capacity growth, or grid/electrification constraints. No buy/sell view is implied. Expanded the universe around the physical AI data-center chokepoint with five US-listed or US-traded names outside the core seed list. The strongest additions cluster around medium-voltage switchgear, mechanical/electrical contracting, data-center cooling equipment, rack-level liquid cooling, and water/fluid-management adjacencies. This pass intentionally excludes already-seeded leaders such as Vertiv, Eaton, GE Vernova, Quanta Services, and hyperscalers.
